title.zh: 卷三百五十七 列傳第一百十六 何灌 李熙靖 王雲 譚世勣 梅執禮 程振 劉延慶
title.en: Volume 357 Biographies 116: He Guan, Li Xijing, Wang Yun, Tan Shiji, Mei Zhili, Cheng Zhen, Liu Yanqing
title.raw: 卷三百五十七 列傳第一百十六 何灌 李熙靖 王雲 譚世勣 梅執禮 程振 劉延慶 Volume 357 Biographies 116: He Guan, Li Xijing, Wang Yun, Tan Shiji, Mei Zhili, Cheng Zhen, Liu Yanqing

sentences.zh: 何灌 李熙靖 王雲 譚世勣 梅執禮 程振 劉延慶

translations.literal: He Guan, Li Xijing, Wang Yun, Tan Shiji, Mei Zhili, Cheng Zhen, Liu Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: He Guan, Li Xijing, Wang Yun, Tan Shiji, Mei Zhili, Cheng Zhen, and Liu Yanqing.

sentences.zh: 何灌，字仲源，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: He Guan, styled Zhongyuan, was a man of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He Guan, styled Zhongyuan, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 武選登第，為河東從事。

translations.literal: He passed the military selection examination and became an aide in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the military selection examination and served as an aide in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 經略使韓縝雖數試其材，而常沮抑之，不假借。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioner Han Zong, though he repeatedly tested his talent, often held him back and did not lend him support.
translations.idiomatic: Although the frontier commissioner Han Zong repeatedly tested his abilities, he regularly held him back and never gave him a fair chance.

sentences.zh: 久乃語之曰：「君奇士也，他日當據吾坐。

translations.literal: After a long while he finally said to him: "You are an extraordinary man; one day you will occupy my seat."
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he finally told him, "You are an extraordinary man. One day you will sit in my place."

sentences.zh: 」為府州、火山軍巡檢。

translations.literal: He served as patrol inspector of Fuzhou and Huoshan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed patrol inspector of Fuzhou and the Huoshan Army.

sentences.zh: 盜蘇延福狡悍，為二邊患，灌親梟其首。

translations.literal: The bandit Su Yanfu was cunning and fierce and a scourge on both frontiers; Guan personally beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Su Yanfu was cunning and fierce, a menace on both borders, and Guan personally cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 賈胡疃有泉，遼人常越境而汲，灌親申畫界堠，遏其來，忿而舉兵犯我。

translations.literal: At Jiahu Tuan there was a spring; Liao people often crossed the border to draw water. Guan personally demarcated the boundary markers to block them. Angered, they raised troops and invaded us.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiahu Tuan there was a spring that Liao subjects often crossed the border to use. Guan personally marked out the boundary posts to stop them. Enraged, they raised an army and attacked our territory.

sentences.zh: 灌迎高射之，發輒中，或著崖石皆沒鏃，敵驚以為神，逡巡斂去。

translations.literal: Guan met them and shot from high ground; every shot hit, and those that struck cliff rocks buried the arrowheads entirely. The enemy were amazed and thought it supernatural; after hesitating they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guan met them and shot from higher ground. Every arrow found its mark, and those that struck cliff faces buried their heads deep in the rock. The enemy were awestruck and took it for divine skill; after a pause they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後三十年，契丹蕭太師與灌會，道曩事，數何巡檢神射，灌曰：「即灌是也。

translations.literal: Thirty years later the Khitan Grand Master Xiao met with Guan and spoke of past events, repeatedly praising Patrol Inspector He's miraculous archery. Guan said: "That was I, Guan."
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years later the Khitan Grand Master Xiao met Guan and spoke of old times, repeatedly praising Patrol Inspector He's uncanny marksmanship. Guan said, "That man was I."

sentences.zh: 」蕭矍然起拜。

translations.literal: Xiao started up in astonishment and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao started up in astonishment and bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 為河東將，與夏人遇，鐵騎來追，灌射皆徹甲，至洞胸出背，疊貫後騎，羌懼而引卻。

translations.literal: As a Hedong general he encountered the Xia. Iron cavalry pursued; Guan's shots all pierced armor, some passing through the chest and out the back and striking several riders in succession. The Qiang feared and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as a Hedong general, he met the Xia in battle. Iron cavalry pressed the pursuit, but Guan's arrows pierced every coat of mail, some passing clean through a man's chest and out his back and striking several riders in a row. The Qiang were terrified and fell back.

sentences.zh: 知甯化軍、豐州，徙熙河都監，見童貫不拜，貫憾焉。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Ninghua Army and Fengzhou, then was transferred to inspector-general of Xihe. When he met Tong Guan he did not bow, and Tong resented this.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Ninghua Army and Fengzhou, then was transferred to inspector-general of Xihe. When he met Tong Guan he did not bow, and Tong took offense.

sentences.zh: 張康國薦于徽宗，召對，問西北邊事，以笏畫禦榻，指坐衣花紋為形勢。

translations.literal: Zhang Kangguo recommended him to Emperor Huizong. Summoned for audience, he was asked about northwest frontier affairs; he used his tablet to trace on the imperial couch and pointed to the flower patterns on the seated robe as terrain features.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kangguo recommended him to Emperor Huizong. Called to audience and questioned about northwest frontier affairs, he traced on the imperial couch with his tablet and used the flower patterns on the Emperor's robe to illustrate the terrain.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「敵在吾目中矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The enemy is already within my sight."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The enemy is already plain before my eyes."

sentences.zh: 提點河東刑獄，遷西上閣門使、領威州刺史、知滄州。

translations.literal: As judicial intendant of Hedong he was promoted to West Upper Gate envoy, concurrently prefect of Weizhou, and administrator of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as judicial intendant of Hedong, he was promoted to West Upper Gate envoy, given concurrent charge of Weizhou, and made administrator of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以治城鄣功，轉引進使。

translations.literal: For merit in repairing walls and fortifications, he was transferred to Introducing Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements in repairing walls and fortifications, he was transferred to the post of Introducing Envoy.

sentences.zh: 詔運粟三十萬石於並塞三州，灌言：「水淺不勝舟，陸當用車八千乘，沿邊方登麥，願以運費增價就糴之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered transporting three hundred thousand piculs of grain to the three border prefectures of Bing. Guan said: "The water is too shallow for boats; overland transport would require eight thousand cartloads. The frontier is just entering the wheat harvest; I request using the transport costs to buy grain locally at an increased price."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered three hundred thousand piculs of grain transported to the three border prefectures of Bing. Guan said, "The water is too shallow for boats, and overland transport would require eight thousand carts. The frontier is just entering the wheat harvest. I ask that the transport costs be used instead to buy grain locally at a higher price."

sentences.zh: 」奏上，報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and approved.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was submitted and approved.

sentences.zh: 安撫使忌之，劾雲板築未畢而冒賞，奪所遷官，仍再貶秩，罷去。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner envied him and impeached him for claiming reward before cloud-plank construction was complete, stripped him of his promoted office, further reduced his rank twice, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner envied him and impeached him for claiming reward before the cloud-plank fortifications were finished. He was stripped of his newly granted office, demoted two more ranks, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知岷州，引邈川水溉間田千頃，湟人號廣利渠。

translations.literal: Before long he was made prefect of Minzhou; he channeled Miaochuan water to irrigate a thousand mu of scattered fields, and the people of Huang called it the Broad Benefit Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made prefect of Minzhou. He diverted Miaochuan water to irrigate a thousand mu of scattered fields, and the people of Huang called the channel the Broad Benefit Canal.

sentences.zh: 徙河州，復守岷，提舉熙河蘭湟弓箭手。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hezhou, then again defended Min, and directed the Xihe, Lan, and Huang archer corps.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hezhou, then returned to defend Min and was put in charge of the Xihe, Lan, and Huang archer corps.

sentences.zh: 入言：「漢金城、湟中谷斛八錢，今西寧、湟、廓即其地也，漢、唐故渠尚可考。

translations.literal: He entered court and said: "In Han times grain in Jincheng and Huangzhong sold for eight cash per picul. Present Xining, Huang, and Kuo are that very region, and Han and Tang canals can still be traced."
translations.idiomatic: He went to court and said, "In Han times grain in Jincheng and Huangzhong sold for eight cash per picul. Present-day Xining, Huang, and Kuo occupy that same region, and the old Han and Tang canals can still be traced."

sentences.zh: 若先葺渠引水，使田不病旱，則人樂應募，而射士之額足矣。

translations.literal: If we first repair the canals and bring water so the fields are not afflicted by drought, people will gladly enlist, and the quota of archer soldiers will be filled.
translations.idiomatic: If we first repair the canals and bring in water so the fields are spared drought, people will gladly enlist, and the quota of archer soldiers will be filled.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: His advice was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 甫半歲，得善田二萬六千頃，募士七千四百人，為他路最。

translations.literal: In barely half a year he gained twenty-six thousand mu of fertile fields and recruited seventy-four hundred soldiers, the highest of any circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In barely half a year he brought under cultivation twenty-six thousand mu of good land and recruited seventy-four hundred soldiers, the highest total of any circuit.

sentences.zh: 童貫用兵西邊，灌取古骨龍馬進武軍，加吉州防禦使，改知蘭州。

translations.literal: When Tong Guan campaigned on the western frontier, Guan took Gugulong and entered Jinwu Army; he was made defender of Jizhou and transferred to administer Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan campaigned on the western frontier, Guan captured Gugulong and entered Jinwu Army. He was made defender of Jizhou and transferred to administer Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又攻仁多泉城，炮傷足不顧，卒拔城，斬首五百級。

translations.literal: He also attacked Rendequan city; wounded in the foot by cannon fire he paid no heed, ultimately captured the city, and beheaded five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Rendequan city. Though wounded in the foot by cannon fire, he paid no attention and finally took the city, beheading five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 尋改廓州防禦使。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made defender of Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made defender of Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，劉法陷於敵，震武危甚，熙帥劉仲武使灌往救。

translations.literal: Early in the Xuanhe era Liu Fa fell to the enemy, Zhenwu was gravely endangered, and the Xi commander Liu Zhongwu sent Guan to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuanhe era Liu Fa was lost to the enemy and Zhenwu was in grave danger, so the Xi commander Liu Zhongwu sent Guan to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 灌以眾寡不敵，但張虛聲駭之，夏人宵遁。

translations.literal: Guan, outnumbered, merely raised a false show of force to frighten them, and the Xia fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Guan merely put on a show of force to frighten them, and the Xia withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 灌恐覘其實，遽反兵，仲武猶奏其逗遛，罷為淮西鈐轄。

translations.literal: Guan feared they would spy out the truth and hurriedly turned his troops back. Zhongwu still memorialized that he had dallied, and he was dismissed to serve as Huai West commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the enemy would discover how weak he really was, Guan hurriedly turned his army back. Zhongwu still memorialized that he had dragged his feet, and he was removed from office and made Huai West commander.

sentences.zh: 從平方臘，獲賊帥呂師囊，遷同州觀察使、浙東都鈐轄，改浙西。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Fang La, he captured the rebel leader Lü Shichong; he was promoted to military commissioner of Tongzhou and Eastern Zhejiang commander, then transferred to Western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Fang La and captured the rebel leader Lü Shichong. He was promoted to military commissioner of Tongzhou and commander of Eastern Zhejiang, then transferred to Western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 童貫北征，檄統制兵馬，涿、易平，以知易州，遷甯武軍承宣使、燕山路副都總管，又加龍、神衛都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Tong Guan marched north, Guan was ordered to command troops; Zhuo and Yi were pacified; he was made administrator of Yizhou; he was promoted to Ningwu Army commissioner and deputy overall commander of Yan Road, and then also made commander-in-chief of the Dragon and Divine Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan marched north, Guan was ordered to take command of the troops. After Zhuo and Yi were pacified he was made administrator of Yizhou, promoted to Ningwu Army commissioner and deputy overall commander of Yan Road, and then also made commander-in-chief of the Dragon and Divine Guards.

sentences.zh: 夔離不取景州，圍薊州。

translations.literal: Aguda did not take Jingzhou and instead besieged Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Aguda did not take Jingzhou and instead besieged Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 貫諉以兵事，即復景城，釋薊圍。

translations.literal: Tong Guan blamed him with military responsibility; he immediately recovered Jing city and lifted the siege of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan blamed him for the military situation, whereupon he immediately recovered Jing city and lifted the siege of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 郭藥師統蕃、漢兵，灌白：「頃年折氏歸朝，朝廷別置一司，專部漢兵，至於克行，乃許同營。

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi commanded Tangut and Han troops. Guan advised: "When the Zhe clan submitted years ago, the court set up a separate office solely to command Han troops; only at Kexing were they allowed to camp together."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi commanded both Tangut and Han troops. Guan advised, "When the Zhe clan submitted years ago, the court set up a separate office to command Han troops alone. Only at Kexing were the two allowed to camp together."

sentences.zh: 今但宜令藥師主常勝軍，而以漢兵委灌輩。

translations.literal: Now Yaoshi alone should command the Ever-Victorious Army, and Han troops should be entrusted to us.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yaoshi alone should command the Ever-Victorious Army, and the Han troops should be entrusted to men like myself.

sentences.zh: 」貫不聽。

translations.literal: Tong Guan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 召還，管幹步軍司。

translations.literal: He was recalled to manage the Bureau of Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to manage the Bureau of Infantry.

sentences.zh: 陪遼使射玉津園，一發破的，再發則否。

translations.literal: Accompanying a Liao envoy shooting at Jade Ford Garden, his first shot hit the target; the second did not.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying a Liao envoy in archery at Jade Ford Garden, his first shot hit the target, but the second did not.

sentences.zh: 客曰：「太尉不能耶？

translations.literal: The guest said: "Can the Grand Marshal not do it?"
translations.idiomatic: The guest said, "Can the Grand Marshal not do it?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「非也，以禮讓客耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "It is not that; I was simply deferring to our guest."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "It is not that. I was simply yielding to our guest out of courtesy."

sentences.zh: 」整弓復中之，觀者誦歎，帝親賜酒勞之。

translations.literal: He readied his bow and hit again; onlookers chanted praise, and the Emperor personally bestowed wine to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: He readied his bow and hit the target again. The onlookers broke into admiring cries, and the Emperor personally bestowed wine to reward him.

sentences.zh: 遷步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was promoted to infantry vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commander of the infantry.

sentences.zh: 金師南下，悉出禁旅付梁方平守黎陽。

translations.literal: As the Jin armies marched south, all palace troops were sent with Liang Fangping to hold Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin armies marched south, all the palace troops were sent out under Liang Fangping to hold Liyang.

sentences.zh: 灌謂宰相白時中曰：「金人傾國遠至，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Guan told the Grand Councilor Bai Shizhong: "The Jurchens have come from afar with their whole nation; their attack cannot be withstood."
translations.idiomatic: Guan told Grand Councilor Bai Shizhong, "The Jurchens have come from afar with their whole nation behind them. Their onslaught cannot be withstood."

sentences.zh: 今方平掃精銳以北，萬有一不枝梧，何以善吾後，盍留以衛根本。

translations.literal: Now Fangping sweeps the elite north; if by any chance they cannot hold, how can we secure our rear? Better to keep troops to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Now Fangping is sweeping the elite troops north. If by any chance they cannot hold, how will we secure our rear? We ought to keep forces here to guard the capital itself."

sentences.zh: 」不從，明日，又命灌行，辭以軍不堪戰，強之，拜武泰軍節度使、河東河北制置副使。

translations.literal: They did not heed him. The next day Guan was again ordered to march; he declined, saying the army could not fight; forced to go, he was appointed military commissioner of Wutai Army and deputy frontier commissioner of Hedong and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: They did not listen. The next day Guan was ordered to march again. He declined on the grounds that the army was unfit for battle, but was forced to go and was appointed military commissioner of Wutai Army and deputy frontier commissioner of Hedong and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 未及行而帝內禪，灌領兵入衛。

translations.literal: Before he could depart the Emperor abdicated, and Guan led troops to guard the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could set out the Emperor abdicated, and Guan led troops in to guard the palace.

sentences.zh: 鄆王楷至門欲入，灌曰：「大事已定，王何所受命而來？

translations.literal: Prince Yun Wang Kai came to the gate wishing to enter. Guan said: "Great affairs are already settled; by what commission does Your Highness come?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yun Wang Kai came to the gate wishing to enter. Guan said, "The great matter is already settled. By what commission does Your Highness come?"

sentences.zh: 」導者懼而退。

translations.literal: The guide feared and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The guide was frightened and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 灌竟行，援兵二萬不能足，聽募民充數。

translations.literal: Guan ultimately marched; the relief force of twenty thousand could not be filled, and he was permitted to recruit civilians to make up the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Guan set out all the same, but the relief force of twenty thousand could not be filled, and he was permitted to recruit civilians to make up the numbers.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年正月二日，次滑州，方平南奔，灌亦望風迎潰。

translations.literal: On the second day of the first month of the first year of Jingkang he halted at Huazhou; Fangping fled south, and Guan also collapsed before the wind.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the first month of the first year of Jingkang he halted at Huazhou. Fangping fled south, and Guan too broke before the enemy's advance.

sentences.zh: 黃河南岸無一人禦敵，金師遂直叩京城。

translations.literal: South of the Yellow River not a single man resisted the enemy, and the Jin armies went straight to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yellow River not a single man stood to resist the enemy, and the Jin armies marched straight on the capital.

sentences.zh: 灌至，乞入見，不許，而令控守西隅。

translations.literal: When Guan arrived he begged for an audience but was denied, and was ordered to hold the west sector.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan arrived he begged for an audience but was refused, and was ordered to hold the western sector of the defenses.

sentences.zh: 背城拒戰凡三日，被創，沒於陣，年六十二。

translations.literal: Fighting with his back to the wall for three days, he was wounded and died in battle at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with his back to the wall for three days, was wounded, and died in battle at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 帳下韓綜、雷彥興，奇士也，各手殺數人，從以死。

translations.literal: Under his command Han Zong and Lei Yanxing, extraordinary men, each killed several with their own hands and died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Under his command were Han Zong and Lei Yanxing, both extraordinary men. Each killed several enemies with his own hands and died with him.

sentences.zh: 欽宗哀悼，賜金帛，命官護葬。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong mourned him, bestowed gold and silk, and ordered officials to escort the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong mourned him, bestowed gold and silk, and ordered officials to escort the funeral.

sentences.zh: 已而言者論其不守河津，追削官秩。

translations.literal: Later critics argued that he had failed to hold the river crossing, and his ranks were posthumously stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Later critics argued that he had failed to hold the river crossing, and his ranks were posthumously stripped.

sentences.zh: 長子薊，至閣門宣贊舍人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ji rose to the post of Gate Proclamation Registrar of the Inner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ji rose to the post of Gate Proclamation Registrar of the Inner Gate.

sentences.zh: 從父戰，箭貫左臂，拔出之，病創死。

translations.literal: Following his father into battle, an arrow pierced his left arm; he pulled it out and died of the wound.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father into battle. An arrow pierced his left arm; he pulled it out and died of the wound.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，中子蘚以灌事泣訴於朝，詔復履正大夫、忠正軍承宣使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing his second son Xian wept before the court over Guan's case, and an edict restored Lüzheng Daifu and Zhongzheng Army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaoxing his second son Xian wept before the court over Guan's case, and an edict restored his ranks of Lüzheng Daifu and Zhongzheng Army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 李熙靖

translations.literal: Li Xijing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xijing

sentences.zh: 李熙靖，字子安，常州晉陵人，唐衛公德裕九世孫也。

translations.literal: Li Xijing, styled Zi'an, was a man of Jinling in Changzhou and the ninth-generation descendant of Tang Duke of Wei Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xijing, styled Zi'an, was a native of Jinling in Changzhou and a ninth-generation descendant of Tang Duke of Wei Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 祖均、父公弼皆進士第。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jun and his father Gongbi both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun and his father Gongbi both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 公弼，崇甯初通判潞州，以議三舍法不便，使者劾其沮格詔令，坐削黜以死。

translations.literal: Gongbi, early in the Chongning era as deputy prefect of Lu, because he argued that the Three Hall system was inconvenient, envoys impeached him for obstructing edicts; he was demoted and died in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi, early in the Chongning era while serving as deputy prefect of Lu, argued that the Three Hall system was inconvenient. Envoys impeached him for obstructing edicts, and he was demoted and died in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 熙靖擢第，又中詞學兼茂，選為辟雍錄、太學正，升博士。

translations.literal: Xijing passed the examinations and also passed the Polished Literary Learning examination; he was selected as director of the Imperial College and senior examiner, then promoted to erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing passed the examinations and also passed the Polished Literary Learning examination. He was selected as director of the Imperial College and senior examiner, then promoted to erudite.

sentences.zh: 以父老丐外，除提舉淮東學事便養，命下，乃得河東；

translations.literal: Citing his aged father, he sought an exterior post and was appointed education commissioner of Huai East for convenient care of his parents; when the order came down he received Hedong instead.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his aged father, he sought a post outside the capital and was appointed education commissioner of Huai East so he could care for his parents nearby. When the order came down, however, he received Hedong instead.

sentences.zh: 而為淮東者，臧祐之也。

translations.literal: The one appointed to Huai East was Zang Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The man appointed to Huai East was Zang Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 蓋省吏取祐之賂，輒易之。

translations.literal: A provincial clerk had taken a bribe from Youzhi and switched the appointments.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial clerk had taken a bribe from Youzhi and switched the appointments.

sentences.zh: 或教使自言，熙靖曰：「事君不擇地，吾其可發人之私，求自便也？

translations.literal: Someone urged him to speak up for himself. Xijing said: "In serving one's lord one does not choose place—how could I expose another man's secret to seek my own convenience?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him to speak up for himself. Xijing said, "In serving one's lord one does not choose the place of service. How could I expose another man's secret just to seek my own convenience?"

sentences.zh: 」宰相聞而賢之，留為兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: The grand councilor heard of this and esteemed him; he was retained as vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: The grand councilor heard of this and admired him, and he was kept at court as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂去，還，為右司員外郎。

translations.literal: On his father's death he left office; when he returned he served as vice director of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father's death he left office. When he returned he served as vice director of the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 王黼乙太宰領應奉司，又方事燕雲，立經撫房於中書獨專之，他執政皆不得預。

translations.literal: Wang Fu, as Grand Chancellor, also headed the Tribute Service; focused on Yan-Yun affairs, he established a frontier pacification office in the Central Secretariat and kept sole control of it, while the other chief ministers could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu, as Grand Chancellor, also headed the Tribute Service. With Yan-Yun affairs his main concern, he established a frontier pacification office in the Central Secretariat and kept sole control of it, while the other chief ministers were excluded.

sentences.zh: 熙靖與言曰：「應奉之職，非宰相所當預。

translations.literal: Xijing spoke to him and said: "The Tribute Service is not a duty a chancellor should oversee."
translations.idiomatic: Xijing spoke to him and said, "The Tribute Service is not a duty a chancellor should oversee."

sentences.zh: 尚書、樞密皆有兵房，足以治疆事，經撫何為者哉？

translations.literal: The ministries and the Military Affairs Commission both have military offices sufficient to handle frontier affairs—what need is there for a frontier pacification office?
translations.idiomatic: The ministries and the Military Affairs Commission both have military offices sufficient to handle frontier affairs. What need is there for a frontier pacification office?"

sentences.zh: 」黼積不樂。

translations.literal: Fu grew increasingly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Fu grew increasingly displeased.

sentences.zh: 同列五人皆躐躋禁從，獨滯留四年。

translations.literal: Five colleagues all leaped into forbidden attendant posts, while he alone stagnated for four years.
translations.idiomatic: Five colleagues all vaulted into high attendant posts, while he alone remained stuck in place for four years.

sentences.zh: 都水丞失職，移過於熙靖，貶其兩秩，又將左轉為國子司業，執政交言不可，僅遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: When a director of waterways lost his post through negligence, the blame was shifted to Xijing; he was demoted two ranks and was about to be transferred down to vice director of the Imperial University, but the chief ministers protested that this would not do, and he was only moved to vice director of rituals.
translations.idiomatic: When a director of waterways lost his post through negligence, the blame was shifted to Xijing. He was demoted two ranks and was about to be transferred down to vice director of the Imperial University, but the chief ministers protested, and he was only moved to vice director of rituals.

sentences.zh: 黼罷，乃拜中書舍人，蔡攸又惡之，出知拱州。

translations.literal: When Fu fell from power, Xijing was appointed Secretariat drafter; Cai You also hated him and had him sent out to administer Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu fell from power, Xijing was appointed Secretariat drafter. Cai You also hated him and had him sent out to administer Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 越兩月，復以故官召，入對言：「燕山雖定，宜益謹思患豫防之戒。

translations.literal: Two months later he was recalled to his former office; at audience he said: "Although the Yan Mountains are settled, we should be all the more careful in guarding against trouble beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: Two months later he was recalled to his former office. At audience he said, "Although the Yan Mountains are settled, we should be all the more careful to guard against trouble before it comes."

sentences.zh: 」徽宗曰：「《詩》所謂'迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖戶'者是也。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong said: "As the Odes say, 'Before heaven's rain clouds gather, gather mulberry bark and line window and door'—that is the idea."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong said, "That is what the Odes mean when they say, 'Before heaven's rain clouds gather, gather mulberry bark and line window and door.'"

sentences.zh: 」熙靖進曰：「孔子云：'為此詩者，其知道乎！

translations.literal: Xijing advanced and said: "Confucius said: 'The composer of this poem—did he know the Way!"
translations.idiomatic: Xijing advanced and said, "Confucius said, 'The composer of this poem—did he know the Way!

sentences.zh: 能治其國家，誰敢侮之？

translations.literal: Who can govern his state yet be insulted?'"
translations.idiomatic: Who can govern his state well and still be insulted?'"

sentences.zh: '願陛下為無疆之計。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would plan for boundless security."
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty would plan for lasting security without limit."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，同譚世勣事龍德宮，改顯謨閣待制、提舉醴泉觀。

translations.literal: Early in the Jingkang era he served Longde Palace together with Tan Shiji; he was made Xianmo Pavilion attendant and director of Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang era he served Longde Palace together with Tan Shiji. He was made Xianmo Pavilion attendant and director of Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 道君待之甚厚，常從容及內禪事，曰：「外人以為吳敏功，殊不知此自出吾意耳，吾苟不欲，人言且滅族，誰敢哉？

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor treated him very generously and often spoke at ease of the abdication, saying: "Outsiders credit Wu Min, but they do not know this came from my own intent. If I had not wished it, speech would have meant extermination of my clan—who would have dared?"
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor treated him very generously and often spoke at ease of the abdication. He said, "Outsiders credit Wu Min, but they do not know this came from my own intent. If I had not wished it, any word against it would have meant the destruction of my clan. Who would have dared?"

sentences.zh: 或謂吾似唐睿宗上畏天戒，故為之，吾有此心久矣。

translations.literal: Some say I resemble Tang Ruizong yielding from fear of heaven's warning, but I had this in mind long ago."
translations.idiomatic: Some say I resemble Tang Ruizong yielding from fear of heaven's warning, but I had this in mind long ago."

sentences.zh: 」熙靖再拜賀。

translations.literal: Xijing bowed twice in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing bowed twice in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 敏聞而忌之，以進對不時受罰。

translations.literal: Min heard of this and resented it; Xijing was penalized for an untimely audience.
translations.idiomatic: Min heard of this and resented it, and Xijing was penalized for an untimely audience.

sentences.zh: 既拒張邦昌之命，憂憤廢食，家人進粥藥寬譬之，終無生意。

translations.literal: Having refused Zhang Bangchang's commission, he was so grief-stricken and angry that he stopped eating; his family brought porridge and medicine to comfort him, but in the end he had no will to live.
translations.idiomatic: Having refused Zhang Bangchang's commission, he was so grief-stricken and angry that he stopped eating. His family brought porridge and medicine to comfort him, but in the end he had no will to live.

sentences.zh: 故人視其病，相持啜泣，索筆書唐王維所賦「百官何日再朝天」之句，明日遂卒，年五十三，與世勣同贈端明殿學士。

translations.literal: An old friend visited him in his illness; they wept holding each other. He asked for a brush and wrote the line from Wang Wei's poem, "When will officials again attend court?" The next day he died at the age of fifty-three, and together with Shiji was posthumously made an academician of the Hall of Endpointal Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: An old friend visited him in his illness, and they wept holding each other. He asked for a brush and wrote the line from Wang Wei's poem, "When will the officials again attend court at dawn?" The next day he died at the age of fifty-three. Together with Shiji he was posthumously made an academician of the Hall of Endpointal Brightness.

sentences.zh: 王雲，字子飛，澤州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yun, styled Zifei, was a man of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, styled Zifei, was a native of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 父獻可，仕至英州刺史、知瀘州。

translations.literal: His father Xianke served to the posts of prefect of Yingzhou and administrator of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianke served to the posts of prefect of Yingzhou and administrator of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 黃庭堅謫於涪，獻可遇之甚厚，時人稱之。

translations.literal: When Huang Tingjian was exiled to Fu, Xianke treated him very generously, and people of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Tingjian was exiled to Fu, Xianke treated him very generously, and people of the time praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 雲舉進士，從使高麗，撰《雞林志》以進。

translations.literal: Yun passed the jinshi examination, accompanied a mission to Goryeo, and composed Records of Goguryeo Chicken Forest and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yun passed the jinshi examination, accompanied a mission to Goryeo, and composed Records of Goguryeo Chicken Forest, which he submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 擢秘書省校書郎，出知簡州，遷陝西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to collator in the Secretariat and sent out to administer Jianzhou, then transferred to vice commissioner of Shaanxi transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to collator in the Secretariat, sent out to administer Jianzhou, and then transferred to vice commissioner of Shaanxi transport.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，從童貫宣撫幕，入為兵部員外郎、起居中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era he served on Tong Guan's pacification staff, then entered court as vice minister of war and drafting attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanhe era he served on Tong Guan's pacification staff, then entered court as vice minister of war and drafting attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，以給事中使斡離不軍，議割三鎮以和。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang he was sent as supervising censor to Wolibu's army to negotiate ceding the three prefectures for peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang he was sent as supervising censor to Wolibu's army to negotiate the cession of the three prefectures in exchange for peace.

sentences.zh: 使還，傳道斡離不之意，以為黏罕得朝廷所與餘睹蠟書，堅雲中國不可信，欲敗和約。

translations.literal: On his return he relayed Wolibu's message, saying that Nianhan had obtained the wax-sealed letter the court had sent to Yutu and firmly declared that Song China could not be trusted, and wished to break the peace treaty.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he relayed Wolibu's message: Nianhan had obtained the wax-sealed letter the court had sent to Yutu and insisted that Song China could not be trusted, and now wished to break the peace treaty.

sentences.zh: 執政以為不然，罷為徽猷閣待制、知唐州。

translations.literal: The chief ministers did not believe this, and he was dismissed to serve as Huiyao Pavilion attendant and administrator of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers did not believe him, and he was dismissed to serve as Huiyao Pavilion attendant and administrator of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 金人陷太原，召拜刑部尚書，再出使，許以三鎮賦入之數。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens took Taiyuan he was summoned and appointed minister of justice, sent on another mission, and permitted to offer the tax revenue of the three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens took Taiyuan he was summoned and appointed minister of justice, sent on another mission, and authorized to offer the tax revenue of the three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 雲至真定，遣從吏李裕還言：「金人不復求地，但索五輅及上尊號，且須康王來，和好乃成。

translations.literal: Yun reached Zhending and sent his attendant Li Yu back with the message: "The Jurchens no longer demand territory, but only ask for the five imperial carriages and an honorific title for the Emperor, and moreover require Prince Kang to come before peace can be concluded."
translations.idiomatic: Yun reached Zhending and sent his attendant Li Yu back with word that the Jurchens no longer demanded territory, but only wanted the five imperial carriages and an honorific title for the Emperor, and that Prince Kang must come in person before peace could be concluded.

sentences.zh: 」欽宗悉從之，且命王及馮澥往。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong agreed to all of this and ordered the Prince and Feng Xi to go.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong agreed to everything and ordered the Prince and Feng Xi to go.

sentences.zh: 未行，而車輅至長垣，為所卻，雲亦還。

translations.literal: Before they set out the imperial carriages reached Changyuan and were turned back, and Yun also returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could set out the imperial carriages reached Changyuan and were turned back, and Yun returned as well.

sentences.zh: 澥奏言雲誕妄誤國，雲言：「事勢中變，金人必欲得三鎮，不然，則進兵取汴都。

translations.literal: Xi memorialized that Yun's wild falsehoods had harmed the state. Yun said: "The situation has changed midway; the Jurchens must have the three prefectures, or else they will advance and take Bian capital."
translations.idiomatic: Xi memorialized that Yun's reckless falsehoods had harmed the state. Yun said, "The situation has changed midway. The Jurchens will insist on having the three prefectures, or else they will advance and take the capital at Bian."

sentences.zh: 」中外震駭，詔集百官議，雲固言：「康王舊與斡離不結歡，宜將命。

translations.literal: Court and country were shaken; an edict summoned all officials to deliberate. Yun firmly said: "Prince Kang once formed friendly ties with Wolibu and should carry the commission."
translations.idiomatic: Court and country were shaken, and an edict summoned all officials to deliberate. Yun insisted, "Prince Kang once formed friendly ties with Wolibu and should carry the commission."

sentences.zh: 」帝慮為所留，雲曰：「和議既成，必無留王之理，臣敢以百口保之。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared the Prince would be detained. Yun said: "Once peace is concluded there can be no reason to detain the Prince. I dare guarantee this with the lives of my whole household."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor feared the Prince would be detained. Yun said, "Once peace is concluded there can be no reason to detain the Prince. I stake the lives of my whole household on it."

sentences.zh: 」王遂受命，而雲以資政殿學士為之副。

translations.literal: The Prince then accepted the commission, and Yun served as his deputy in the capacity of Zizheng Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince then accepted the commission, with Yun serving as his deputy in the capacity of Zizheng Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 頃雲奉使過磁、相，勸兩郡徹近城民舍，運粟入保，為清野之計，民怨之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yun went on mission through Ci and Xiang, he urged both prefectures to demolish dwellings near the cities, transport grain into fortified places, and adopt a scorched-earth policy, and the people resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yun went on mission through Ci and Xiang, he urged both prefectures to demolish dwellings near the cities, move grain into fortified places, and adopt a scorched-earth policy. The people resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 及是，次磁州，又與守臣宗澤有憾。

translations.literal: On this occasion, when they halted at Cizhou, he also had a grudge against the defending official Zong Ze.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, when they halted at Cizhou, he also had a grudge against the defending official Zong Ze.

sentences.zh: 於是王出謁嘉應神祠，雲在後，民遮道諫曰：「肅王已為金人所留，王不宜北去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince went out to pay respects at the Jiaying Spirit Shrine with Yun behind him. The people blocked the road and remonstrated: "Prince Su has already been detained by the Jurchens; Your Highness should not go north."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Prince went out to pay respects at the Jiaying Spirit Shrine with Yun following behind. The people blocked the road and remonstrated, "Prince Su has already been detained by the Jurchens. Your Highness should not go north."

sentences.zh: 」厲聲指雲曰：「清野之人，真奸賊也。

translations.literal: They shouted and pointed at Yun: "This man of the scorched-earth policy is a true traitor."
translations.idiomatic: They shouted and pointed at Yun, "This man of the scorched-earth policy is a true traitor."

sentences.zh: 」王出廟行，或發雲笥，得烏絁短巾，蓋雲夙有風眩疾，寢則以護首者。

translations.literal: As the Prince left the shrine and set out, someone opened Yun's trunk and found a black silk headcloth; Yun had long suffered from vertigo and used it to protect his head when sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince left the shrine and set out, someone opened Yun's trunk and found a black silk headcloth. Yun had long suffered from vertigo and wore it to protect his head when he slept.

sentences.zh: 民益信其為奸，噪而殺之。

translations.literal: The people were all the more convinced he was a traitor, raised a clamor, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The people were all the more convinced he was a traitor. They raised a clamor and killed him.

sentences.zh: 王見事勢洶洶，乃南還相州。

translations.literal: The Prince, seeing how turbulent matters had become, turned south and returned to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how turbulent matters had become, the Prince turned south and returned to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是役也，雲不死，王必北行，議者以是驗天命雲。

translations.literal: In this affair, had Yun not died the Prince would certainly have gone north; commentators took this as proof that Heaven had ordained Yun's death.
translations.idiomatic: In this affair, had Yun not died the Prince would certainly have gone north. Commentators took this as proof that Heaven had ordained Yun's death.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，贈觀文殿學士。

translations.literal: Early in the Jianyan era he was posthumously made Guanwen Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era he was posthumously made Guanwen Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 雲兄霽，崇甯時，為謀議司詳議官，上書告蔡京罪，黥隸海島。

translations.literal: Yun's elder brother Ji, during the Chongning era, served as detailed reviewer in the Policy Deliberation Office, submitted a memorial accusing Cai Jing of crimes, and was tattooed and exiled to an island.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's elder brother Ji, during the Chongning era, served as detailed reviewer in the Policy Deliberation Office. He submitted a memorial accusing Cai Jing of crimes and was tattooed and exiled to an island.

sentences.zh: 欽宗復其官，從種師中戰死。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong restored his office; he followed Zhong Shizhong and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong restored his office. He followed Zhong Shizhong and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 譚世勣

translations.literal: Tan Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Shiji

sentences.zh: 譚世勣字彥成，潭州長沙人。

translations.literal: Tan Shiji, styled Yancheng, was a man of Changsha in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Shiji, styled Yancheng, was a native of Changsha in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，教授郴州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as instructor in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as instructor in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時王氏學盛行，世勣雅不喜。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Anshi's learning was flourishing, and Shiji had never liked it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Anshi's learning was in full vogue, and Shiji had never cared for it.

sentences.zh: 或問之，曰：「說多而屢變，無不易之論也。

translations.literal: When someone asked him about it he said: "Its doctrines are many and constantly changing; there is no settled teaching that does not change."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked him about it he said, "Its doctrines are many and constantly changing. There is no settled teaching that does not shift."

sentences.zh: 」置其書不觀。

translations.literal: He put their books aside and did not read them.
translations.idiomatic: He put their books aside and would not read them.

sentences.zh: 又中詞學兼茂科，除秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He also passed the Polished Literary Learning examination and was appointed corrector in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also passed the Polished Literary Learning examination and was appointed corrector in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時相蔡京子攸領書局，同舍郎多翕附以取貴仕。

translations.literal: At the time Chancellor Cai Jing's son You headed the book bureau, and many fellow secretaries fawned on him to obtain high office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chancellor Cai Jing's son You headed the book bureau, and many fellow secretaries fawned on him to obtain high office.

sentences.zh: 世勣獨坐直廬，繙書竟日。

translations.literal: Shiji alone sat in the duty hall and read books all day.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji alone sat in the duty hall and read books all day long.

sentences.zh: 梁師成之客與為鄰居，數致師成願交意，謝不答。

translations.literal: A client of Liang Shicheng lived nearby and repeatedly conveyed Liang's wish to become acquainted; Shiji declined and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: A client of Liang Shicheng lived nearby and repeatedly conveyed Liang's wish to become acquainted. Shiji declined and did not respond.

sentences.zh: 在館六年不遷，京罷，用久次為司門員外郎。

translations.literal: He spent six years in the bureau without promotion; when Jing fell from power Shiji was appointed vice director of the Gate Office by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: He spent six years in the bureau without promotion. When Jing fell from power Shiji was appointed vice director of the Gate Office by seniority.

sentences.zh: 又三年，遷吏部。

translations.literal: Three years later he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 京復相，嫌不附己，罷提點太平宮。

translations.literal: When Jing returned as chancellor he resented that Shiji did not support him and dismissed him to director of Taiping Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing returned as chancellor he resented that Shiji did not support him and dismissed him to the post of director of Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，復還吏部。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he returned to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 幸臣妄引恩澤任子，持不與。

translations.literal: A favored minister falsely invoked an imperial grace to appoint his son to office, and Shiji refused to approve it.
translations.idiomatic: A favored minister falsely invoked an imperial grace to appoint his son to office, and Shiji refused to approve it.

sentences.zh: 吏白有某例，世勣曰：「豈當以暫例破成法！

translations.literal: The clerks reported that there was a precedent. Shiji said: "How can a temporary precedent be used to break established law!"
translations.idiomatic: The clerks reported that there was a precedent. Shiji said, "How can a temporary precedent be used to break established law!"

sentences.zh: 」已而取中旨行之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward an edict from the inner court was obtained and the appointment was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict from the inner court was obtained and the appointment was carried out anyway.

sentences.zh: 進少府監，擢中書舍人，以謹命令、惜名器、廣言路、吝賜予、正上供、省浮費六事言於上，又為當路所嫉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Palace Workshop and then elevated to Secretariat drafter. He spoke to the throne on six matters—strict commands, cherishing offices, broadening the avenue of remonstrance, restraining grants, correcting tribute deliveries, and reducing wasteful spending—and again aroused the jealousy of those in power.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Palace Workshop and then elevated to Secretariat drafter. He spoke to the throne on six matters: strict commands, cherishing offices, broadening the avenue of remonstrance, restraining grants, correcting tribute deliveries, and reducing wasteful spending. Once again he aroused the jealousy of those in power.

sentences.zh: 以徽猷閣待制知婺州，未行，復留之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Huiyao Pavilion attendant and administrator of Wuzhou, but before he set out he was kept at court again.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Huiyao Pavilion attendant and administrator of Wuzhou, but before he could set out he was kept at court again.

sentences.zh: 徽宗禪位東幸，且還，使與李熙靖副執政奉迎，遂同主管龍德宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong abdicated and traveled east, and then returned, Shiji and Li Xijing were made deputies to the chief ministers to welcome him back, and together they supervised Longde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong abdicated and traveled east, and then returned, Shiji and Li Xijing were made deputies to the chief ministers to welcome him back, and together they took charge of Longde Palace.

sentences.zh: 請辨正宣仁國史之謗，述欽聖遺旨以復瑤華，大享神祖仍用富弼侑食，釋奠先聖不當以王安石配，後皆施行。

translations.literal: He requested that the slanders in Empress Xuanren's official history be corrected, set forth Empress Qinsheng's final instructions to restore Consort Yaohua, that the grand sacrifice to Emperor Shenzong still use Fu Bi as attendant spirit, and that Wang Anshi should not be enshrined with the Sage at the Confucian sacrifice—all of which were later carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the slanders in Empress Xuanren's official history be corrected, set forth Empress Qinsheng's final instructions to restore Consort Yaohua, that the grand sacrifice to Emperor Shenzong still use Fu Bi as attendant spirit, and that Wang Anshi should not be enshrined with the Sage at the Confucian sacrifice. All of these proposals were later carried out.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，彗出東方，大臣或謂此四夷將衰之兆，世勣面奏：「垂象可畏，當修德以應天，不宜惑諛說。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn a comet appeared in the east. Some ministers said this was a sign that the four barbarians would decline. Shiji addressed the throne in person: "Heaven's signs are to be feared; we should cultivate virtue to respond to Heaven and should not be misled by flattery."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn a comet appeared in the east. Some ministers said this was a sign that the four barbarians would decline. Shiji addressed the throne in person, "Heaven's signs are to be feared. We should cultivate virtue to respond to Heaven and must not be misled by flattery."

sentences.zh: 」進給事中兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising censor and concurrent reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising censor and concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 內侍喧爭殿門，詔以贖論，世勣駁其不恭，因言：「童貫輩初亦甚微，小惡不懲，將馴至大患。

translations.literal: Inner attendants quarreled noisily at the palace gate; an edict ordered that the matter be settled by payment of a fine. Shiji rebutted this as disrespectful and said: "Men like Tong Guan were at first very insignificant; if small wrongs are not punished, they will gradually grow into great calamities."
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants quarreled noisily at the palace gate, and an edict ordered that the matter be settled by payment of a fine. Shiji rebutted this as disrespectful and said, "Men like Tong Guan were at first very insignificant. If small wrongs are not punished, they will gradually grow into great calamities."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，同類側目。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, his colleagues glared at him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, his colleagues glared at him.

sentences.zh: 何栗建議分外郡為四道，置都總管，事得顓決。

translations.literal: He Li proposed dividing the outer prefectures into four circuits, appointing overall commanders with sole decision-making power.
translations.idiomatic: He Li proposed dividing the outer prefectures into four circuits and appointing overall commanders with sole decision-making power.

sentences.zh: 世勣言：「裂天下以付四人，而王畿所治者才十六縣，獨無尾大不掉之慮乎？

translations.literal: Shiji said: "To split the realm among four men while the imperial domain governs only sixteen counties—is there no fear of a tail too heavy to wag?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiji said, "To split the realm among four men while the imperial domain governs only sixteen counties—is there no fear of a tail too heavy to wag?"

sentences.zh: 」栗不樂。

translations.literal: Li was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Li was displeased.

sentences.zh: 改禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 金騎駸駸南下，世勣言：「守邊為上策；

translations.literal: As Jin cavalry pressed swiftly south, Shiji said: "Defending the frontier is the best strategy;"
translations.idiomatic: As Jin cavalry pressed swiftly south, Shiji said, "Defending the frontier is the best strategy;

sentences.zh: 今邊不得守，守河則京畿自固，中策也；

translations.literal: now that the frontier cannot be held, defending the river will naturally secure the capital region—this is the middle strategy;
translations.idiomatic: now that the frontier cannot be held, defending the river will naturally secure the capital region. That is the middle strategy;

sentences.zh: 巡幸江、淮，會東南兵以捍敵，下策也。

translations.literal: touring the Yangzi and Huai and gathering southeastern troops to resist the enemy is the worst strategy.
translations.idiomatic: touring the Yangzi and Huai and gathering southeastern troops to resist the enemy is the worst strategy.

sentences.zh: 金人既渡河，又請遣大將秦元以所部京畿保甲，分護國門，使兵勢連屬，首尾相援，即金人不敢逼。

translations.literal: Once the Jurchens had crossed the river, he also requested that the great general Qin Yuan be sent with his capital-region militia to guard the city gates in sections, so that military strength would be linked head to tail and mutually support one another, and then the Jurchens would not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jurchens had crossed the river, he also requested that the great general Qin Yuan be sent with his capital-region militia to guard the city gates in sections, so that military strength would be linked from end to end and mutually support one another. Then the Jurchens would not dare press close.

sentences.zh: 孫傅深然之，又格于栗議。

translations.literal: Sun Fu strongly agreed, but the proposal was blocked by Li's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu strongly agreed, but the proposal was blocked by Li's faction.

sentences.zh: 再扈車駕至金帥帳，以十害說其用事者，言講解之利，詞意忠激，金人聳聽。

translations.literal: He again accompanied the imperial carriage to the Jin commander's tent and set forth ten harms to those in power there, speaking of the benefits of negotiated settlement; his words were loyal and impassioned, and the Jurchens listened with rapt attention.
translations.idiomatic: He again accompanied the imperial carriage to the Jin commander's tent and set forth ten harms to those in power there, speaking of the benefits of negotiated settlement. His words were loyal and impassioned, and the Jurchens listened with rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌僭國，令與李熙靖同直學士院，皆稱疾臥不起，以憂卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne he was ordered to serve in the Hanlin Academy together with Li Xijing; both claimed illness and would not rise, and Shiji died of grief at the age of fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne he was ordered to serve in the Hanlin Academy together with Li Xijing. Both claimed illness and would not rise. Shiji died of grief at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，褒其守節，贈端明殿學士。

translations.literal: Early in the Jianyan era his steadfast integrity was praised and he was posthumously made an academician of the Hall of Endpointal Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era his steadfast integrity was praised, and he was posthumously made an academician of the Hall of Endpointal Brightness.

sentences.zh: 梅執禮

translations.literal: Mei Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Zhili

sentences.zh: 梅執禮，字和勝，婺州浦江人。

translations.literal: Mei Zhili, styled Hesheng, was a man of Pujiang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Zhili, styled Hesheng, was a native of Pujiang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調常山尉未赴，以薦為敕令刪定官、武學博士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as magistrate of Changshan but did not take up the post; through recommendation he became an editor of edicts and commands and military academy erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as magistrate of Changshan but did not take up the post. Through recommendation he became an editor of edicts and commands and military academy erudite.

sentences.zh: 大司成強淵明賢其人，為宰相言，相以未嘗識面為慊。

translations.literal: Grand director Qiang Yuanming admired him and spoke of him to the chancellor, who regretted that he had never met him in person.
translations.idiomatic: Grand director Qiang Yuanming admired him and spoke of him to the chancellor, who regretted that he had never met him in person.

sentences.zh: 執禮聞之曰：「以人言而得，必以人言而失，吾求在我者而已。

translations.literal: When Zhili heard this he said: "What is gained through others' words can be lost through others' words; I seek only what depends on myself."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhili heard this he said, "What is gained through others' words can be lost through others' words. I seek only what depends on myself."

sentences.zh: 」卒不往謁。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never went to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 曆軍器、鴻臚丞，比部員外郎，比部職勾稽財貨，文牘山委，率不暇經目。

translations.literal: He served as aide in the Armory and in the Office of Ceremonial; as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's comparison bureau, whose duty was to audit goods and funds, documents piled up like mountains and generally no one had time to examine them.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide in the Armory and in the Office of Ceremonial, then as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's comparison bureau, whose duty was to audit goods and funds. Documents piled up like mountains and generally no one had time to examine them.

sentences.zh: 苑吏有持茶券至為錢三百萬者，以楊戩旨意迫取甚急。

translations.literal: A garden official presented a tea certificate redeemable for three million cash and, acting on Yang Jian's orders, pressed for payment with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: A garden official presented a tea certificate redeemable for three million cash and, acting on Yang Jian's orders, pressed for payment with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 執禮一閱，知其妄，欲白之，長貳疑不敢，乃獨列上，界詐也。

translations.literal: Zhili read it once and knew it was fraudulent; he wished to report it, but his superiors hesitated and dared not act, so he alone submitted a memorial declaring it a fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili read it once and knew it was fraudulent. He wished to report it, but his superiors hesitated and dared not act, so he alone submitted a memorial declaring it a fraud.

sentences.zh: 改度支、吏部，進國子司業兼資善堂翊善，遷左司員外郎，擢中書舍人、給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the revenue and personnel bureaus, promoted to vice director of the Imperial University and concurrent tutor in the Hall of Goodness, moved to vice director of the Left Office, and elevated to Secretariat drafter and supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the revenue and personnel bureaus, promoted to vice director of the Imperial University and concurrent tutor in the Hall of Goodness, moved to vice director of the Left Office, and elevated to Secretariat drafter and supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 林攄以前執政赴闕宿留，冀復故職，執禮論去之。

translations.literal: Lin Shu, a former chief minister, came to the capital and lingered, hoping to recover his old office; Zhili memorialized to have him removed.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shu, a former chief minister, came to the capital and lingered, hoping to recover his old office. Zhili memorialized to have him removed.

sentences.zh: 孟昌齡居鄆質人屋，當贖不肯與，而請中旨奪之，外郡卒留役中都者萬數，肆不逞為奸，詔悉令還，楊戩占不遣；

translations.literal: Meng Changling lived in a house in Yun pledged to another man and, when it came time to redeem it, refused to surrender it, yet requested an inner-court edict to seize it; tens of thousands of conscripts from outer prefectures remained in service in the capital and ran wild committing crimes—an edict ordered them all sent home, but Yang Jian kept them and would not release them;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Changling lived in a house in Yun pledged to another man and, when it came time to redeem it, refused to surrender it, yet requested an inner-court edict to seize it. Tens of thousands of conscripts from outer prefectures remained in service in the capital and ran wild committing crimes. An edict ordered them all sent home, but Yang Jian kept them and would not release them.

sentences.zh: 內侍張佑董葺太廟，僭求賞：皆駁奏弗行。

translations.literal: the inner attendant Zhang You oversaw repairs to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and presumptuously sought reward—all were rebutted in memorials and not approved.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Zhang You oversaw repairs to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and presumptuously sought reward. Zhili rebutted all of these in memorials and none were approved.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 素與王黼善，黼嘗置酒其第，誇示園池妓妾之盛，有驕色。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Wang Fu. Fu once held a banquet at his residence and displayed the splendor of his gardens, ponds, and courtesans with a proud air.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been on good terms with Wang Fu. Fu once held a banquet at his residence and displayed the splendor of his gardens, ponds, and courtesans with a proud air.

sentences.zh: 執禮曰：「公為宰相，當與天下同憂樂。

translations.literal: Zhili said: "As chancellor you should share the worries and joys of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Zhili said, "As chancellor you should share the worries and joys of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今方臘流毒吳地，瘡痍未息，是豈歌舞宴樂時乎？

translations.literal: Now Fang La's poison is spreading through Wu territory and the wounds have not yet healed—is this a time for song, dance, and feasting?
translations.idiomatic: Now Fang La's poison is spreading through Wu territory and the wounds have not yet healed. Is this a time for song, dance, and feasting?"

sentences.zh: 」退又戒之以詩。

translations.literal: On leaving he also admonished him with a poem.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving he also admonished him with a poem.

sentences.zh: 黼愧怒，會孟饗原廟後至，以顯謨閣待制知蘄州，又奪職。

translations.literal: Fu was ashamed and angry; when Zhili arrived late for the sacrifice at the Original Temple, he was made Xianmo Pavilion attendant and administrator of Qizhou, and then stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was ashamed and angry. When Zhili arrived late for the sacrifice at the Original Temple, he was made Xianmo Pavilion attendant and administrator of Qizhou, and then stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙滁州，復集英殿修撰。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Chuzhou and restored as compiler in the Hall for Assembling Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Chuzhou and restored as compiler in the Hall for Assembling Excellence.

sentences.zh: 時賦鹽虧額，滁亦苦抑配。

translations.literal: At the time salt tax quotas fell short, and Chuzhou also suffered from forced apportionment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time salt tax quotas fell short, and Chuzhou also suffered from forced apportionment.

sentences.zh: 執禮曰：「郡不能當蘇、杭一邑，而食鹽乃倍粟數，民何以堪？

translations.literal: Zhili said: "This prefecture is not equal to a single district of Su or Hang, yet the salt levy is double the grain quota—how can the people bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhili said, "This prefecture is not equal to a single district of Su or Hang, yet the salt levy is double the grain quota. How can the people bear it?"

sentences.zh: 」請於朝，詔損二十萬，滁人德之。

translations.literal: He petitioned the court, and an edict reduced the levy by two hundred thousand; the people of Chu were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the court, and an edict reduced the levy by two hundred thousand. The people of Chu were grateful.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，徙知鎮江府，召為翰林學士，道除吏部尚書，旋改戶部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne Zhili was transferred to administer Zhenjiang Prefecture, summoned as Hanlin academician, appointed minister of personnel en route, and soon transferred to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne Zhili was transferred to administer Zhenjiang Prefecture, summoned as Hanlin academician, appointed minister of personnel en route, and soon transferred to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 方軍興，調度不足，執禮請以禁內錢隸有司，凡六宮廩給，皆由度支乃得下。

translations.literal: With war underway supplies were insufficient; Zhili requested that inner-palace funds be placed under regular offices, so that all provisions for the six palaces had to pass through the revenue bureau before disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: With war underway supplies were insufficient. Zhili requested that inner-palace funds be placed under regular offices, so that all provisions for the six palaces had to pass through the revenue bureau before disbursement.

sentences.zh: 嘗有小黃門持中批詣部取錢，而封識不用璽，既悟其失，復取之。

translations.literal: Once a junior eunuch came to the ministry with an inner-court draft to withdraw funds, but the seal on the wrapper was not the imperial seal; realizing the error, he took it back.
translations.idiomatic: Once a junior eunuch came to the ministry with an inner-court draft to withdraw funds, but the seal on the wrapper was not the imperial seal. Realizing the error, he took it back.

sentences.zh: 執禮奏審，詔責典寶夫人而杖黃門。

translations.literal: Zhili memorialized for investigation; an edict rebuked the lady keeper of the seals and had the eunuch beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili memorialized for investigation. An edict rebuked the lady keeper of the seals and had the eunuch beaten.

sentences.zh: 金人圍京都，執禮勸帝親征，而請太上帝后、皇后、太子皆出避，用事者沮之。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens besieged the capital Zhili urged the Emperor to lead the campaign in person and requested that the Retired Emperor, Empress Dowager, Empress, and Crown Prince all leave to take refuge; those in power blocked this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens besieged the capital Zhili urged the Emperor to lead the campaign in person and requested that the Retired Emperor, Empress Dowager, Empress, and Crown Prince all leave to take refuge. Those in power blocked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 洎失守，金人質天子，邀金帛以數百千萬計，曰：「和議已定，但所需滿數，則奉天子還闕。

translations.literal: When the city fell the Jurchens held the Son of Heaven hostage and demanded gold and silk in the tens of millions, saying: "Peace is already settled; once the full amount is supplied the Son of Heaven will be returned to the palace."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the Jurchens held the Son of Heaven hostage and demanded gold and silk in the tens of millions, saying, "Peace is already settled. Once the full amount is supplied the Son of Heaven will be returned to the palace."

sentences.zh: 」執禮與同列陳知質、程振、安扶皆主根索，四人哀民力已困，相與謀曰：「金人所欲無藝極，雖銅鐵亦不能給，盍以軍法結罪，儻窒其求。

translations.literal: Zhili, together with his colleagues Chen Zhizhi, Cheng Zhen, and An Fu, all directed the search for funds. The four men grieved that the people's strength was already exhausted and consulted together: "The Jurchens' demands know no limit; even copper and iron could not satisfy them—why not use military law to fix culpability and perhaps block their demands?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhili, together with his colleagues Chen Zhizhi, Cheng Zhen, and An Fu, all directed the search for funds. The four men grieved that the people's strength was already exhausted and consulted together, "The Jurchens' demands know no limit. Even copper and iron could not satisfy them. Why not use military law to fix culpability and perhaps block their demands?"

sentences.zh: 」而宦者挾宿怨語金帥曰：「城中七百萬戶，所取未百一，但許民持金銀換粟麥，當有出者。

translations.literal: But eunuchs bearing old grudges told the Jin commander: "There are seven million households in the city; what has been taken is not yet one in a hundred. Just allow the people to exchange gold and silver for grain and wheat, and contributions will come forth."
translations.idiomatic: But eunuchs bearing old grudges told the Jin commander, "There are seven million households in the city. What has been taken is not yet one in a hundred. Just allow the people to exchange gold and silver for grain and wheat, and contributions will come forth."

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: Soon afterward it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward it proved so.

sentences.zh: 酋怒，呼四人責之，對曰：「天子蒙塵，臣民皆願致死，雖肝腦不計，于金繒何有哉？

translations.literal: The chieftain was enraged and summoned the four men to rebuke them. They replied: "The Son of Heaven suffers in exile; officials and people all wish to die for the cause—even livers and brains are not counted; what of gold and silk?"
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain was enraged and summoned the four men to rebuke them. They replied, "The Son of Heaven suffers in exile. Officials and people all wish to die for the cause. Even livers and brains are not counted. What of gold and silk?"

sentences.zh: 顧比屋枵空，亡以塞命耳。

translations.literal: Only every household is empty and hollow; there is nothing with which to fulfill the command.
translations.idiomatic: Only every household is empty and hollow. There is nothing with which to fulfill the command.

sentences.zh: 」酋問官長何在，振恐執禮獲罪，遂前曰：「皆官長也。

translations.literal: The chieftain asked where the chief officials were. Zhen, fearing Zhili would be punished, stepped forward and said: "We are all chief officials."
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain asked where the chief officials were. Zhen, fearing Zhili would be punished, stepped forward and said, "We are all chief officials."

sentences.zh: 」酋益怒，先取其副胡舜陟、胡唐老、姚舜明、王俁，各杖之百。

translations.literal: The chieftain grew still angrier and first seized his deputies Hu Shunzhi, Hu Tanglao, Yao Shunming, and Wang Hou, beating each a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain grew still angrier and first seized his deputies Hu Shunzhi, Hu Tanglao, Yao Shunming, and Wang Hou, beating each a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 執禮等猶為之請，俄遣還，將及門，呼下馬撾殺之，而梟其首，時靖康二年二月也。

translations.literal: Zhili and the others still pleaded for them; soon they were sent back, and just as they reached the gate they were called down from their horses, beaten to death, and their heads displayed. This was in the second month of the second year of Jingkang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili and the others still pleaded for them. Soon they were sent back, and just as they reached the gate they were called down from their horses, beaten to death, and their heads displayed. This was in the second month of the second year of Jingkang.

sentences.zh: 是日，天宇晝冥，士庶皆隕涕憤歎。

translations.literal: That day the sky darkened at noon, and officials and commoners all wept tears of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky darkened at noon, and officials and commoners all wept tears of grief and indignation.

sentences.zh: 初，車駕再出，執禮與宗室子昉、諸將吳革等謀集兵奪萬勝門，夜搗金帥帳，迎二帝以歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the imperial carriage went out again, Zhili, together with the imperial clansman Zifang and the generals Wu Ge and others, plotted to gather troops, seize Wansheng Gate, raid the Jin commander's tent by night, and bring the two emperors back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the imperial carriage went out again, Zhili, together with the imperial clansman Zifang and the generals Wu Ge and others, plotted to gather troops, seize Wansheng Gate, raid the Jin commander's tent by night, and bring the two emperors back.

sentences.zh: 而王時雍、徐秉哲使範瓊泄其謀，故不克。

translations.literal: But Wang Shiyong and Xu Bingzhe had Fan Qiong reveal the plot, and so it failed.
translations.idiomatic: But Wang Shiyong and Xu Bingzhe had Fan Qiong reveal the plot, and so it failed.

sentences.zh: 死時，年四十九。

translations.literal: At his death he was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，詔贈通奉大夫、端明殿學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne an edict posthumously granted him Tongfeng Daifu and academician of the Hall of Endpointal Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, an edict posthumously granted him the ranks of Tongfeng Daifu and academician of the Hall of Endpointal Brightness.

sentences.zh: 議者以為薄，復加資政殿學士。

translations.literal: Commentators thought this too meager, and he was further made Zizheng Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators thought this too meager, and he was further made Zizheng Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 程振，字伯起，饒州樂平人。

translations.literal: Cheng Zhen, styled Boqi, was a man of Leping in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhen, styled Boqi, was a native of Leping in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 少有軼材，入太學，一時名輩多從之遊。

translations.literal: In youth he had extraordinary talent; he entered the Imperial College, and many leading men of the time associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had extraordinary talent. He entered the Imperial College, and many leading men of the time sought his company.

sentences.zh: 徽宗幸學，以諸生右職除官，為辟雍錄，升博士，遷太常博士，提舉京東、西路學事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong visited the college, Zhen, as a student of outstanding merit, was granted office; he served as director of the Imperial College, was promoted to erudite, transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and directed education in the eastern and western circuits of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong visited the college, Zhen, as a student of outstanding merit, was granted office. He served as director of the Imperial College, was promoted to erudite, transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and directed education in the eastern and western circuits of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 請立廟于鄒祀孟軻，以公孫醜、萬章、樂正克等配食，從之。

translations.literal: He requested that a temple be established at Zou to sacrifice to Mencius, with Gongsun Chou, Wan Zhang, Yuezheng Ke, and others as attendant spirits, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that a temple be established at Zou to sacrifice to Mencius, with Gongsun Chou, Wan Zhang, Yuezheng Ke, and others as attendant spirits, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 提舉京西常平，入為膳部員外郎、監察御史、辟雍國子司業、左司員外郎兼太子舍人。

translations.literal: He directed the western capital-region granary reserve, then entered court as vice director in the Board of Provisions, investigating censor, vice director of the Imperial College and National University, and vice director of the Left Office concurrently attendant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the western capital-region granary reserve, then entered court as vice director in the Board of Provisions, investigating censor, vice director of the Imperial College and National University, and vice director of the Left Office concurrently attendant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 始至，即言：「古者大祭禮登餕受爵，必以上嗣，既《禮經》所載，且元豐彝典具存。

translations.literal: As soon as he arrived he said: "In antiquity at the great sacrifice, when ascending to receive the sacrificial meat and accept the cup, the heir apparent had to be present. This is recorded in the Book of Rites, and the Yuanfeng canonical regulations still survive intact."
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he arrived he said, "In antiquity at the great sacrifice, when ascending to receive the sacrificial meat and accept the cup, the heir apparent had to be present. This is recorded in the Book of Rites, and the Yuanfeng canonical regulations still survive intact.

sentences.zh: 昨天子展事明堂，而殿下不預，非所以尊宗廟、重社稷也。

translations.literal: Yesterday the Son of Heaven performed the rites at the Bright Hall, yet Your Highness did not participate—this is not the way to honor the ancestral temples and esteem the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the Son of Heaven performed the rites at the Bright Hall, yet Your Highness did not participate. This is not the way to honor the ancestral temples and esteem the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 」太子矍然曰：「宮僚初無及此者。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince started and said: "None of the palace staff had ever raised this."
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince started and said, "None of the palace staff had ever raised this."

sentences.zh: 」由是特加獎異。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was specially praised and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was specially praised and favored.

sentences.zh: 方臘起，振謂王黼宜乘此時建革天下弊事，以上當天意，下順人心。

translations.literal: When Fang La rose in rebellion Zhen told Wang Fu that he ought to seize this moment to reform the world's abuses, thereby answering Heaven above and winning hearts below.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La rose in rebellion Zhen told Wang Fu that he ought to seize this moment to reform the abuses of the realm, thereby answering Heaven above and winning hearts below.

sentences.zh: 黼不懌，曰：「上且疑黼挾寇，奈何？

translations.literal: Fu was displeased and said: "The Emperor already suspects that Fu is exploiting the bandits—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu was displeased and said, "The Emperor already suspects that I am exploiting the bandits. What can be done?"

sentences.zh: 」振知黼忌其言，趨而出，然太子薦之甚力，遂擢給事中。

translations.literal: Zhen knew Fu resented his words and hurried out, but the Crown Prince recommended him vigorously, and he was elevated to supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen knew Fu resented his words and hurried out, but the Crown Prince recommended him vigorously, and he was elevated to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 黼白振資淺，且雅長書命，請以為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Fu reported that Zhen's seniority was shallow and that he excelled at drafting documents, and requested that he be made Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Fu reported that Zhen's seniority was shallow and that he excelled at drafting documents, and requested that he be made Secretariat drafter instead.

sentences.zh: 侍郎馮熙載出知亳州，黼怨熙載，欲振詆以醜語，振不肯。

translations.literal: Vice minister Feng Xizai was sent out to administer Bozhou; Fu resented Xizai and wanted Zhen to slander him with ugly words, but Zhen refused.
translations.idiomatic: Vice minister Feng Xizai was sent out to administer Bozhou. Fu resented Xizai and wanted Zhen to slander him with ugly words, but Zhen refused.

sentences.zh: 黼使言者劾為黨，罷提舉沖佑觀。

translations.literal: Fu had critics impeach him as a factional partisan, and he was dismissed to director of Chongyou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had critics impeach him as a factional partisan, and he was dismissed to the post of director of Chongyou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 居三年，復還故官。

translations.literal: After three years he returned to his former office.
