translations.idiomatic: After three years he returned to his former office.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，進吏部侍郎，為欽宗言：「柄臣不和，論議多駁，詔令輕改，失於事幾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang he was promoted to vice minister of personnel and told Emperor Qinzong: "The chief ministers are not in harmony, deliberations are often overturned, and edicts are lightly changed—this misses the critical moment in affairs."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang he was promoted to vice minister of personnel and told Emperor Qinzong, "The chief ministers are not in harmony, deliberations are often overturned, and edicts are lightly changed. This misses the critical moment in affairs.

sentences.zh: 金人交兵半歲，而至今不解者，以和戰之說未一故也。

translations.literal: The Jurchens have been at war for half a year, yet the conflict remains unresolved because the debate over peace and war has not been settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens have been at war for half a year, yet the conflict remains unresolved because the debate over peace and war has not been settled.

sentences.zh: 裁抑濫賞，如白黑易分，而數月之間，三變其議，以私心不除，各蔽其黨故也。

translations.literal: Restraining excessive rewards should be as easy as distinguishing black from white, yet within a few months the policy changed three times, because private motives were not removed and each man shielded his own faction.
translations.idiomatic: Restraining excessive rewards should be as easy as distinguishing black from white, yet within a few months the policy changed three times, because private motives were not removed and each man shielded his own faction.

sentences.zh: 今日一人言之，以為是而行；

translations.literal: Today one man speaks and it is deemed right and carried out;
translations.idiomatic: Today one man speaks and it is deemed right and carried out;

sentences.zh: 明日一人言之，以為非而止。

translations.literal: tomorrow another speaks and it is deemed wrong and halted.
translations.idiomatic: tomorrow another speaks and it is deemed wrong and halted.

sentences.zh: 或聖斷隃度而不暇疇咨，或大臣偏見而遂形播告，所以動未必善，處未必宜，乃輒為之反汗，其勢不得不爾也。」

translations.literal: Sometimes the sacred decision is made in private without time to consult broadly; sometimes a chief minister's bias is immediately proclaimed abroad. Thus actions are not necessarily good and measures not necessarily fitting, yet they are repeatedly reversed—under such conditions it cannot be otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the sacred decision is made in private without time to consult broadly. Sometimes a chief minister's bias is immediately proclaimed abroad. Thus actions are not necessarily good and measures not necessarily fitting, yet they are repeatedly reversed. Under such conditions it cannot be otherwise."

sentences.zh: 時金兵至河北，振請糾諸道兵掎角擊之，曰：「彼猖獗如此，陛下尚欲守和議，而不使之少有懲艾乎？

translations.literal: At the time Jin troops had reached Hebei; Zhen requested that armies from all circuits be assembled to attack them from converging angles, saying: "They are so rampant—does Your Majesty still wish to uphold the peace agreement and not make them suffer even a little punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jin troops had reached Hebei. Zhen requested that armies from all circuits be assembled to attack them from converging angles, saying, "They are so rampant. Does Your Majesty still wish to uphold the peace agreement and not make them suffer even a little punishment?"

sentences.zh: 」上嗟味其言，而牽於外廷，不能用。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed over his words but was constrained by the outer court and could not act on them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sighed over his words but was constrained by the outer court and could not act on them.

sentences.zh: 拜開封尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 故時，大辟有情可矜，多奏取原貸；

translations.literal: Formerly, in capital cases where there were extenuating circumstances, memorials often sought commutation or pardon;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, in capital cases where there were extenuating circumstances, memorials often sought commutation or pardon;

sentences.zh: 崇寧以來，議者謂輦轂先彈壓，率便文殺之。

translations.literal: since the Chongning era critics said the capital must suppress crime first and generally used expedient documents to execute offenders.
translations.idiomatic: since the Chongning era critics said the capital must suppress crime first and generally used expedient documents to execute offenders.

sentences.zh: 振請復舊制。

translations.literal: Zhen requested restoration of the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen requested restoration of the old system.

sentences.zh: 詔捕亡命卒，得數千人，振請以隸步軍而除其罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the capture of deserters; several thousand were found. Zhen requested that they be assigned to the infantry and their crimes remitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the capture of deserters, and several thousand were found. Zhen requested that they be assigned to the infantry and their crimes remitted.

sentences.zh: 步軍司欲論如法，振曰：「方多事之際，而一日殺數千人，必大駭觀聽。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Infantry wished to punish them according to law. Zhen said: "At a time of many crises, to kill several thousand men in a single day would greatly shock public opinion."
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Infantry wished to punish them according to law. Zhen said, "At a time of many crises, to kill several thousand men in a single day would greatly shock public opinion."

sentences.zh: 」乃盡釋之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were released.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all were released.

sentences.zh: 改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 金騎在郊，邀車駕出城，振為何栗言：「宜思所以折之之策。

translations.literal: Jin cavalry were in the suburbs and demanded that the imperial carriage leave the city. Zhen told He Li: "We should think of a strategy to rebuff them."
translations.idiomatic: Jin cavalry were in the suburbs and demanded that the imperial carriage leave the city. Zhen told He Li, "We should think of a strategy to rebuff them."

sentences.zh: 」栗不從。

translations.literal: Li did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Li did not listen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，及於難，年五十七。

translations.literal: Before long he met disaster at the age of fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he met disaster at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 金人去，從子庭訪得其首歸葬之。

translations.literal: After the Jurchens departed his nephew Ting recovered his head and returned it for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jurchens departed his nephew Ting recovered his head and returned it for burial.

sentences.zh: 初，王黼使其客沈積中圖燕，振戒以後禍，積中懼而言不可。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Fu had his client Shen Jizhong plan the Yan campaign; Zhen warned of future calamity, and Jizhong, fearing, said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Fu had his client Shen Jizhong plan the Yan campaign. Zhen warned of future calamity, and Jizhong, fearing, said it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 既而振乃用是死，聞者痛之。

translations.literal: In the end Zhen died for this very reason, and those who heard of it grieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Zhen died for this very reason, and those who heard of it grieved.

sentences.zh: 初，宣和崇道家之說，振侍坐東宮，從容言：「孔子以《鴟鴞》之詩為知道，其詞不過曰'迨天之未陰雨，綢繆牖戶'而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Xuanhe era when Daoist teachings were honored, Zhen sat in attendance in the Eastern Palace and said at ease: "Confucius held the poem 'Owl' to show knowledge of the Way; its words amount to no more than 'Before heaven's rain clouds gather, gather mulberry bark and line window and door.'"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Xuanhe era when Daoist teachings were honored, Zhen sat in attendance in the Eastern Palace and said at ease, "Confucius held the poem 'Owl' to show knowledge of the Way. Its words amount to no more than 'Before heaven's rain clouds gather, gather mulberry bark and line window and door.'"

sentences.zh: 老子亦云：'為之於未有，治之於未亂。

translations.literal: Laozi also said: 'Act when nothing yet exists; govern before disorder arises.'
translations.idiomatic: Laozi also said, 'Act when nothing yet exists; govern before disorder arises.

sentences.zh: '今不固根本於無事之時，而事目前區區，非二聖人意。

translations.literal: Now if we do not strengthen the root in times of peace but attend only to petty present concerns, this is not the intent of the Two Sages.'
translations.idiomatic: Now if we do not strengthen the root in times of peace but attend only to petty present concerns, this is not the intent of the Two Sages.'"

sentences.zh: 」他日，太子為徽宗道之。

translations.literal: Another day the Crown Prince reported this to Emperor Huizong.
translations.idiomatic: Another day the Crown Prince reported this to Emperor Huizong.

sentences.zh: 徽宗寤，頗欲去健羨，疏左右近習，而宦寺楊戩輩方大興宮室，懼不得肆，因讒家令楊馮，以為將輔太子幸非常。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong awoke to it and wished to remove excess and distance his close attendants, but eunuchs like Yang Jian were then greatly expanding the palace and feared they would not be free to indulge themselves; they therefore slandered the household steward Yang Feng, claiming he would assist the Crown Prince in an irregular coup.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong awoke to it and wished to remove excess and distance his close attendants. But eunuchs like Yang Jian were then greatly expanding the palace and feared they would not be free to indulge themselves. They therefore slandered the household steward Yang Feng, claiming he would assist the Crown Prince in an irregular coup.

sentences.zh: 徽宗震怒，執馮誅之，而太子之言亦廢。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong was greatly enraged, seized Feng and executed him, and the Crown Prince's words were also abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong was greatly enraged, seized Feng and executed him, and the Crown Prince's advice was also abandoned.

sentences.zh: 振尹京時，兩宮方困於惎間，振極意彌縫，治龍德梁忻獄，寬其罪，不使有纖介可指。

translations.literal: When Zhen served as prefect of the capital the two palaces were then troubled by mutual suspicion; Zhen did his utmost to mend matters, handled the Longde Palace case of Liang Xin, lightened the offense, and left not the slightest point that could be seized upon.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen served as prefect of the capital the two palaces were troubled by mutual suspicion. Zhen did his utmost to mend matters, handled the Longde Palace case of Liang Xin, lightened the offense, and left not the slightest point that could be seized upon.

sentences.zh: 劉延慶

translations.literal: Liu Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanqing

sentences.zh: 劉延慶，保安軍人。

translations.literal: Liu Yanqing was a man of Bao'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanqing was a native of Bao'an Army.

sentences.zh: 世為將家，雄豪有勇，數從西伐，立戰功，積官至相州觀察使、龍神衛都指揮使、鄜延路總管。

translations.literal: His family had been military for generations; bold and brave, he repeatedly joined western campaigns, achieved merit in battle, and rose through the ranks to military commissioner of Xiangzhou, commander-in-chief of the Dragon and Divine Guards, and overall commander of Fuyan Road.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been military for generations. Bold and brave, he repeatedly joined western campaigns, achieved merit in battle, and rose through the ranks to military commissioner of Xiangzhou, commander-in-chief of the Dragon and Divine Guards, and overall commander of Fuyan Road.

sentences.zh: 遷泰寧軍節度觀察留後，改承宣使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner and observation commissioner of Taining Army, then made commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner and observation commissioner of Taining Army, then made commissioner.

sentences.zh: 破夏人成德軍，擒其酋賞屈，降王子益麻党征。

translations.literal: He defeated the Xia at Chengde Army, captured their chieftain Shangqu, and received the surrender of the princely scion Yima Dangzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Xia at Chengde Army, captured their chieftain Shangqu, and received the surrender of the princely scion Yima Dangzheng.

sentences.zh: 拜保信軍節度使、馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of Baoxin Army and vice commander-in-chief of the cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of Baoxin Army and vice commander-in-chief of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從童貫平方臘，節度河陽三城。

translations.literal: Following Tong Guan in the pacification of Fang La, he served as military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Following Tong Guan in the pacification of Fang La, he served as military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 又從北伐，以宣撫都統制督兵十萬，渡白溝。

translations.literal: He again joined the northern campaign as overall pacification commander, directing one hundred thousand troops across the Bai Ditch.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the northern campaign as overall pacification commander, directing one hundred thousand troops across the Bai Ditch.

sentences.zh: 延慶行軍無紀律，郭藥師扣馬諫曰：「今大軍拔隊行而不設備，若敵人置伏邀擊，首尾不相應，則望塵決潰矣。

translations.literal: Yanqing marched without discipline. Guo Yaoshi seized his horse's bridle and remonstrated: "The main army is now moving out in column without taking precautions. If the enemy sets an ambush and attacks, with head and tail unable to support each other, the army will break at the mere sight of dust."
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing marched without discipline. Guo Yaoshi seized his horse's bridle and remonstrated, "The main army is now moving out in column without taking precautions. If the enemy sets an ambush and attacks, with head and tail unable to support each other, the army will break at the mere sight of dust."

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He would not listen.

sentences.zh: 至良鄉，遼將蕭幹帥眾來，延慶與戰，敗績，遂閉壘不出。

translations.literal: At Liangxiang the Liao general Xiao Gan led his forces against him; Yanqing fought and was defeated, then shut himself in the fort and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangxiang the Liao general Xiao Gan led his forces against him. Yanqing fought and was defeated, then shut himself in the fort and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 藥師曰：「幹兵不過萬人，今悉力拒伐，燕山必虛，願得奇兵五千，倍道襲取，令公之子三將軍簡師為後繼。

translations.literal: Yaoshi said: "Gan's troops number no more than ten thousand. He is now exerting all his strength to resist us, so Yan Mountains must be empty. I wish to have five thousand picked troops to take a forced march and seize it, with Your Excellency's son the Third General leading a picked force as rear support."
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshi said, "Gan's troops number no more than ten thousand. He is now exerting all his strength to resist us, so Yan Mountains must be empty. Give me five thousand picked troops to take a forced march and seize it, with Your Excellency's son the Third General leading a picked force as rear support."

sentences.zh: 」延慶許之，遣大將高世宣與藥師先行，即入燕城，幹舉精甲三千巷戰。

translations.literal: Yanqing agreed and sent the great general Gao Shixuan with Yaoshi ahead; they entered Yan city, and Gan rallied three thousand elite armored troops for street fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing agreed and sent the great general Gao Shixuan with Yaoshi ahead. They entered Yan city, and Gan rallied three thousand elite armored troops for street fighting.

sentences.zh: 三將軍者，光世也。

translations.literal: The Third General was Guangshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Third General was Guangshi.

sentences.zh: 渝約不至，藥師失援敗走，世宣死之。

translations.literal: He broke the agreement and did not come; Yaoshi lost support, was defeated and fled, and Shixuan died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the agreement and did not come. Yaoshi lost support, was defeated and fled, and Shixuan died in the battle.

sentences.zh: 延慶營于盧溝南，幹分兵斷餉道，擒護糧將王淵，得漢軍二人，蔽其目，留帳中，夜半偽相語曰：「聞漢軍十萬壓吾境，吾師三倍，敵之有餘。

translations.literal: Yanqing camped south of the Lu Ditch. Gan divided his troops to cut the supply route, captured the grain-protecting general Wang Yuan, and took two Han soldiers; he covered their eyes and kept them in his tent. At midnight he feigned conversation: "I hear a hundred thousand Han troops are pressing our border. Our army is three times as large—more than enough to defeat the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing camped south of the Lu Ditch. Gan divided his troops to cut the supply route, captured the grain-protecting general Wang Yuan, and took two Han soldiers. He covered their eyes and kept them in his tent. At midnight he feigned conversation, "I hear a hundred thousand Han troops are pressing our border. Our army is three times as large—more than enough to defeat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 當分左右翼，以精兵沖其中，左右翼為應，殲之無遺。

translations.literal: We should divide into left and right wings, strike the center with elite troops, and have the wings respond—destroy them to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: We should divide into left and right wings, strike the center with elite troops, and have the wings respond. Destroy them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 」陰逸其一人歸報。

translations.literal: Secretly he let one man escape to report back.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he let one man escape to report back."

sentences.zh: 明旦，延慶見火起，以為敵至，燒營而奔，相蹂踐死者百余裏。

translations.literal: At dawn Yanqing saw fires rise and thought the enemy had arrived; he burned his camp and fled, and men trampled one another to death for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yanqing saw fires rise and thought the enemy had arrived. He burned his camp and fled, and men trampled one another to death for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 自熙、豐以來，所儲軍實殆盡。

translations.literal: Since the Xining and Yuanfeng eras the stored military supplies were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xining and Yuanfeng eras the stored military supplies were nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 退保雄州，燕人作賦及歌誚之。

translations.literal: He withdrew to hold Xiongzhou, and the people of Yan composed rhapsodies and songs to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to hold Xiongzhou, and the people of Yan composed rhapsodies and songs to mock him.

sentences.zh: 朝議延慶喪師，不可不行法，坐貶率府率，安置筠州。

translations.literal: The court debated that Yanqing had lost his army and the law could not go unenforced; he was demoted to director of the Rate Office and placed under restraint in Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated that Yanqing had lost his army and the law could not go unenforced. He was demoted to director of the Rate Office and placed under restraint in Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹知中國不能用兵，由是輕宋。

translations.literal: The Khitan knew that China could not use its armies effectively, and from this they came to despise Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan knew that China could not use its armies effectively, and from this they came to despise Song.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為鎮海軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made military commissioner of Zhenhai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made military commissioner of Zhenhai Army.

sentences.zh: 靖康之難，延慶分部守京城，城陷，引秦兵萬人奪開遠門以出，至龜兒寺，為追騎所殺。

translations.literal: During the Jingkang crisis Yanqing divided his forces to defend the capital. When the city fell he led ten thousand Qin troops to seize Kaiyuan Gate and break out; at Guier Temple he was killed by pursuing cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang crisis Yanqing divided his forces to defend the capital. When the city fell he led ten thousand Qin troops to seize Kaiyuan Gate and break out. At Guier Temple he was killed by pursuing cavalry.

sentences.zh: 光世自有傳。

translations.literal: Guangshi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：靖康之變、執禮、振不忍都人塗炭，拒強敵無厭之欲，親逢其凶。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the Jingkang crisis Zhili and Zhen could not bear to see the capital people suffer ruin; they resisted the insatiable demands of a powerful enemy and personally met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: In the Jingkang crisis Zhili and Zhen could not bear to see the people of the capital suffer ruin. They resisted the insatiable demands of a powerful enemy and personally met disaster.

sentences.zh: 熙靖、世勣不肯以一身事二姓，悲不食以終。

translations.literal: Xijing and Shiji refused to serve two dynasties with one body and died from grief without eating.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing and Shiji refused to serve two dynasties with one body and died from grief without eating.

sentences.zh: 灌、延慶戰敗而沒。

translations.literal: Guan and Yanqing were defeated in battle and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Yanqing were defeated in battle and perished.

sentences.zh: 此數人者，其所遭不同，至於死國難則一而已。

translations.literal: These several men encountered different circumstances, yet in dying for the state's crisis they were one.
translations.idiomatic: These several men encountered different circumstances, yet in dying for the state's crisis they were one.

sentences.zh: 雲之死，雖其有以取之，殆亦天未欲絕宋祀也；

translations.literal: As for Yun's death, though he partly brought it on himself, perhaps Heaven also did not yet wish to cut off the sacrifices of Song;
translations.idiomatic: As for Yun's death, though he partly brought it on himself, perhaps Heaven also did not yet wish to cut off the sacrifices of Song;

sentences.zh: 不然，是行也，康王其危哉！

translations.literal: otherwise on that journey Prince Kang would have been in grave danger!
translations.idiomatic: otherwise on that journey Prince Kang would have been in grave danger!
